verdict_reason: Minimal RuntimeException subclass matching the custom-exception pattern in the Spring Boot best-practices bundle and wired to a working 400 bad-request handler; the only issue is a class Javadoc that misdescribes which conditions actually throw it.

todos.issue: Class Javadoc names two triggers that never throw this exception: a missing identity header is rejected inside IdentityHeaderFilter (which writes problem+json itself because @RestControllerAdvice cannot see filter exceptions) and a malformed query parameter surfaces as MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException with its own handler; the sole production throw site is OperatorService.list for an out-of-range page (< 1).
todos.fix: Reword the Javadoc to describe the real trigger (a request parameter that is syntactically valid but out of range, e.g. page < 1) and drop the missing-identity-header and malformed-query-param examples, so nobody throws this from a servlet filter expecting the advice to map it.
